question: What public CvSU route can an independent Bangwit project use to retrieve the Cañas 2017 thesis pages needed to inspect its species list and station context?

officialProcedure.abstractProgram: Search the thesis title/subject in CvSU E-Library and submit the Thesis Abstract request form; the stated deliverable is the thesis abstract. The record already exposes a 16-page abstract/contents scan.
officialProcedure.printedPageProgram: The Online Printed Book Delivery Program is expressly limited to currently enrolled CvSU students, faculty and staff. The page says the library can scan 5-10 pages; it does not document eligibility for an independent non-thesis app project.
officialProcedure.referenceService: The same page lists online reference channels and describes inquiries from students, faculty and staff. It does not clearly establish that an independent project outside CvSU may request thesis pages or use the printed-page service.

decision: Do not submit the abstract form as though it grants the missing full-thesis pages; do not submit a page-delivery request until the library confirms eligibility. Prepare an unsent eligibility inquiry asking whether a community researcher may consult the print thesis in person or request a limited, authorized excerpt.
limitations: The public page does not state whether an independent project outside CvSU may use the in-library thesis collection.
The existing abstract/contents scan is not the full thesis and does not include the summary table or station appendix.
Even an authorized scan limited to 5-10 pages may not provide all methods and station crosswalk details; ask the library what permitted access exists.
No species name or local occurrence may be inferred from the reported 23-fish watershed aggregate.
nextAction: Joseph can review and manually send the draft through an official CvSU library reference channel if desired. In parallel, continue independently sourced fish-evidence review; do not block CALABARZON work on a library response.
